title: The Three-Point Turn (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 106bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist Perth driving
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The three-point turn was three points when I learned to drive in Perth
Since then it's become a five or seven point affair of worth
The street was wider when I was seventeen and so was I
The cars have gotten bigger and the gutters haven't — why

[Pre-Chorus]
A driving examiner once watched me do one and said fine
Which I've been dining out on since nineteen eighty-nine

[Chorus]
The three-point turn knows something I don't know
It knows the geometry of commitment in a row
The three-point turn requires a decision and a follow through
You cannot half do a three-point turn — that much is true
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
Someone always appears when you're halfway through the manoeuvre
A pedestrian, a cyclist, someone walking with a Hoover
They all stand and watch you from the footpath with concern
As if the three-point turn is something they personally learn

[Bridge]
I've been told there's a twelve-point version in certain Japanese cities
Where the streets are built for motorbikes and motorcycles pretty
But I completed mine in three in a cul-de-sac in Nedlands
And I'll take that to the grave along with all my other credentials

[Outro]
Three-point turn knows… geometry of commitment… three-point turn knows
That's my boy
